newsitem.title: ITALY: BOXING-"GRIM REAPER" WINS WBC SUPER-MIDDLE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-"GRIM REAPER" WINS WBC SUPER-MIDDLE TITLE.

text.p: Britain's Robin Reid, nicknamed "The Grim Reaper", won the World Boxing Council (WBC) super-middleweight title on Saturday by stopping Italy's Vincenzo Nardiello in the seventh of 12 scheduled rounds.

The Italian repeatedly claimed that Reid, with his nickname emblazoned on his shorts, had fought a dirty fight but his words rang hollow to many, with the public applauding Reid and whistling Nardiello.
"The referee gave far too much to him, what kind of a referee is he?," the Italian said angrily of highly experienced American official Frank Cappuccino.

Reid, bronze medallist at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics and since then unbeaten, refused to look his opponent in the face before the fight but went straight at the Italian, whose nickname "Ice" was shaved into his nape.
The Italian, making his first title defence after winning the belt from South African Thulane Malinga in July, was briefly on his knees in the second round but avoided a count.
Cappuccino repeatedly warned the Briton, apparently for hitting with the inside of the glove, but refused to be misled by Nardiello's claims of low blows.

Reid got in two good rights at the end of the fourth and Nardiello suddenly looked in trouble in the fifth, penned in on the ropes and then finishing the round on his knees when his opponent caught him flush in the face with a right.

A cut opened over his left eye and Nardiello looked in serious trouble in the sixth. He appealed in vain to the referee when Reid clearly hit him on the back during the round, angering the 6,000 fans present.
The end came in the next round, with the referee stopping the fight with two minutes to go as Nardiello, who had protested a perceived low blow, was caught by a hook.
Reid's win took the 25-year-old's fight record to 22-1-0. Nardiello is now 30-0-5.
